claim: The asymmetric location of stereociliary bundle (hair bundle) on the apical surface of mechanosensory hair cells (HCs) dictates the direction in which a given HC can respond to cues such as sound, head movements, and water pressure.
source: The asymmetric location of stereociliary bundle (hair bundle) on the apical surface of mechanosensory hair cells (HCs) dictates the direction in which a given HC can respond to cues such as sound, head movements, and water pressure.
evidence: This is a general statement about HC function supported by established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: Vestibular sensory organs of the inner ear, the maculae, exhibit a line of polarity reversal (LPR) across which hair bundles are polarized in a mirror-image pattern.
source: Notably, vestibular sensory organs of the inner ear, the maculae, exhibit a line of polarity reversal (LPR) across which, hair bundles are polarized in a mirror-image pattern.
evidence: This describes a known anatomical feature of maculae that is established in the field.

claim: HCs in neuromasts of the zebrafish lateral line system are generated as pairs, and two sibling HCs develop opposite hair bundle orientations.
source: Similarly, HCs in neuromasts of the zebrafish lateral line system are generated as pairs, and two sibling HCs develop opposite hair bundle orientations.
evidence: This is supported by citation to López-Schier et al., 2004 in the Introduction section.

claim: Expression of the transcription factor Emx2 is restricted to only one side of the LPR in the maculae or one of the two sibling HCs in neuromasts.
source: Within these sensory organs, expression of the transcription factor Emx2 is restricted to only one side of the LPR in the maculae or one of the two sibling HCs in neuromasts.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1, 2, 9, and 10.

claim: Emx2 mediates hair bundle polarity reversal in restricted subsets of HCs and generates the mirror-image pattern of the sensory organs.
source: Emx2 mediates hair bundle polarity reversal in these restricted subsets of HCs and generates the mirror-image pattern of the sensory organs.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion supported by loss- and gain-of-function experiments shown throughout the manuscript.

claim: Downstream effectors of Emx2 control bundle polarity cell-autonomously via heterotrimeric G proteins.
source: Downstream effectors of Emx2 control bundle polarity cell-autonomously via heterotrimeric G proteins.
evidence: This is supported by pertussis toxin experiments shown in Figures 7 and 8.

claim: Abnormal positioning of the monocilium in the node and multicilia of ependymal cells lining the brain ventricles can lead to left-right asymmetry defects and hydrocephalus, respectively.
source: Abnormal positioning of the monocilium in the node and multicilia of ependymal cells lining the brain ventricles can lead to left-right asymmetry defects and hydrocephalus, respectively (Tissir et al., 2010; Song et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Tissir et al., 2010 and Song et al., 2010.

claim: The asymmetrical orientation or polarity of hair bundle on top of sensory HCs provides the directional sensitivity for detecting sensory inputs in the form of vibrations.
source: Similarly, the asymmetrical orientation or polarity of hair bundle on top of sensory HCs provides the directional sensitivity for detecting sensory inputs in the form of vibrations (Shotwell et al., 1981).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Shotwell et al., 1981.

claim: Deflection of the hair bundle towards its kinocilium leads to the opening of the mechanotransduction channels located on the tips of stereocilia and depolarizes the HC.
source: Deflection of the hair bundle towards its kinocilium leads to the opening of the mechanotransduction channels located on the tips of stereocilia and depolarizes the HC.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Shotwell et al., 1981 and is established knowledge in the field.

claim: Hair bundle displacement in the opposite direction results in hyperpolarization.
source: Hair bundle displacement in the opposite direction results in hyperpolarization (Figure 1A; Shotwell et al., 1981).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Shotwell et al., 1981 and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: The orientation and positioning of the hair bundle determine the directional sensitivity of the HC.
source: Therefore, the orientation and positioning of the hair bundle determine the directional sensitivity of the HC.
evidence: This is a logical inference from the previous statements about HC function.

claim: Emx2 is expressed in the lateral extrastriola (LES) of the utricle and inner region (IR) of the saccule.
source: Using both in situ hybridization and immunostaining, we found that Emx2 expression is restricted to the lateral extrastriolar region (LES) of the utricle and inner region (IR) of the saccule (Figure 1B,C,C',F,F', Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1 and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The border of the Emx2 expression domain closely follows the LPR in the two maculae.
source: The border of the Emx2 expression domain (Figure 1C',F', green line bordering the green region) closely follows the LPR in the two maculae, at the lateral edge of the oncomodulin-positive striola in the utricle and at the center of the saccule bisecting the striola (blue outlined; Li et al., 2008; Desai et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1 and citations to Li et al., 2008 and Desai et al., 2005.

claim: Only HCs lateral to the LPR in the utricle and internal to the LPR in the saccule are Emx2 positive and they show polarities different from the rest of the maculae.
source: Using this approach, we found that only HCs lateral to the LPR in the utricle and internal to the LPR in the saccule are Emx2 positive and they show polarities different from the rest of the maculae (Figure 1D–E',G–H', arrows).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Emx2 expression is restricted to one side of the LPR in the maculae that share the same hair bundle polarity.
source: These results indicate that Emx2 expression is restricted to one side of the LPR in the maculae that share the same hair bundle polarity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in Figure 1.

claim: The Emx2-lineage domain remained in both maculae of Emx2Cre/-;RosatdT/+ mutant ears.
source: We observed that the Emx2-lineage domain remained in both maculae of Emx2Cre/-;RosatdT/+ mutant ears.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Hair bundle polarity within the Emx2-lineage domain was reversed in Emx2Cre/-;RosatdT/+ mutants compared to controls.
source: The spatial relationship of Emx2-lineage domain with the striola was maintained but hair bundle polarity within the domain was reversed (Figure 2E–H,M–P, green region) compared to controls (Figure 2C,K, green region).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2.

claim: There was no reduction in the size of maculae in Emx2 mutants.
source: We also did not observe a reduction in the size of maculae (Figure 2—source data 1) or total HC number in the utricle (Figure 2—source data 2) of our Emx2 mutants.
evidence: This is supported by quantitative data in Figure 2—source data 1 and 2.

claim: The unidirectional hair bundle phenotype in Emx2-/- maculae is not caused by the loss of a domain.
source: Taken together, our results indicate that the unidirectional hair bundle phenotype in Emx2-/- maculae is not caused by the loss of a domain, rather Emx2 has a role in establishing regional bundle polarity in the maculae.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the lineage tracing and mutant analysis data.

claim: Emx2 has a cell-autonomous role in reversing bundle polarity.
source: Furthermore, the strong correlation between the border of Emx2 immunostaining domain and the LPR suggests that Emx2 has a cell-autonomous role in reversing bundle polarity.
evidence: This is inferred from the correlation between Emx2 expression and hair bundle polarity shown in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: HC precursors in the LES undergo terminal mitosis later than the rest of the maculae.
source: Although our results indicate that HC precursors in the LES (where Emx2 is normally expressed) undergo terminal mitosis later than the rest of the maculae, we did not observe any obvious difference in this timing between controls and Emx2-/- utricles (Figure 3).
evidence: This is supported by EdU labeling experiments shown in Figure 3.

claim: There is no obvious difference in the timing of terminal mitosis between controls and Emx2-/- utricles.
source: Although our results indicate that HC precursors in the LES (where Emx2 is normally expressed) undergo terminal mitosis later than the rest of the maculae, we did not observe any obvious difference in this timing between controls and Emx2-/- utricles (Figure 3).
evidence: This is supported by EdU labeling experiments shown in Figure 3.

claim: Emx2 does not affect hair bundle polarity indirectly via regulating the timing of terminal mitosis of HC precursors in the LES.
source: These results suggest that Emx2 does not affect hair bundle polarity indirectly via regulating the timing of terminal mitosis of HC precursors in the LES.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the EdU labeling data in Figure 3.

claim: In Sox2CreER/+;RosaEmx2/+ mutants with tamoxifen at E12.5/E13.5, the LPR was absent and all hair bundles in the entire utricle were uniformly pointing toward the medial direction.
source: Compared to hair bundles pointing toward the LPR in control utricles (Figure 4A–C), the LPR was absent in GOF-SE early mutants. All hair bundles in the entire utricle were uniformly pointing toward the medial direction (Figure 4D–F,O–Q).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: The ability of ectopic Emx2 to reverse hair bundle polarity is developmentally dependent.
source: This ability of ectopic Emx2 to reverse hair bundle polarity is developmentally dependent.
evidence: This is supported by comparing early (E12.5/E13.5) and late (E15.5/E16.5) tamoxifen administration results shown in Figure 4.

claim: By delaying tamoxifen administration to E15.5 and E16.5, only a partial polarity phenotype was observed in the medial utricle.
source: By delaying the tamoxifen administration to E15.5 and E16.5 (GOF-SE late), at which time many HC precursors have undergone terminal mitosis and started to differentiate (Figure 3), only a partial polarity phenotype was observed in the medial utricle (Figure 4G–I,P–Q, region M).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Once the kinocilium position is established, it no longer responds to Emx2-dependent cues.
source: These results suggest that once the kinocilium position is established, it no longer responds to Emx2-dependent cues.
evidence: This is inferred from the developmental timing experiments shown in Figure 4.

claim: Ectopic expression of Emx2 during early prosensory development resulted in increased apical HC surface area and reduced HC density.
source: Ectopic expression of Emx2 during early prosensory development also resulted in increased apical HC surface area and reduced HC density, which may not be related to the bundle polarity phenotype (Figure 4D–F,M–O).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 4M-O.

claim: In Gfi1Cre/+;RosaEmx2/+ mutant utricles, all HCs in the utricle were pointing towards the medial edge.
source: In Gfi1Cre/+;RosaEmx2/+ mutant utricles (GOF-HC), all HCs in the utricle were pointing towards the medial edge (Figure 4J–L,P–Q) even though the total HC number remained the same (Figure 2—source data 2).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: The hair bundle reversal in the medial utricle of Gfi1Cre/+;RosaEmx2/+ mutants was approximately 180° different from controls.
source: The hair bundle reversal in the medial utricle was approximately 180° different from controls (Figures 4P and 8K, compare region M between control and GOF-HC utricles).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative data shown in Figures 4P and 8K.

claim: In Gfi1Cre/+;RosaEmx2/+ saccules, only the outer region (OR) showed a hair bundle reversal phenotype compared to controls.
source: Similar findings were observed in the saccule: only the outer region (OR) of the saccule where Emx2 is not normally expressed showed a hair bundle reversal phenotype (Figure 5C–D,O) compared to controls (Figure 5A–B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Only a low percentage of Gfi1Cre/+;RosaEmx2/+ maculae retained their oncomodulin staining.
source: Gain-of Emx2 function in naïve HCs also affected some of their endogenous properties since only a low percentage of Gfi1Cre/+;RosaEmx2/+ maculae retained their oncomodulin staining (Figure 5C–D, n = 1/5).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: In Gfi1Cre/+;RosaEmx2/+ ears, hair bundle polarity in both anterior and lateral cristae was reversed compared to controls.
source: In Gfi1Cre/+;RosaEmx2/+ ears, hair bundle polarity in both anterior and lateral cristae was reversed (Figure 5H–J,O) compared to controls (Figure 5E–G).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: No hair bundle polarity abnormality was observed in the cochlea of Gfi1Cre/+;RosaEmx2/+ mutants.
source: As a result, no hair bundle polarity abnormality was observed in the cochlea of Gfi1Cre/+;RosaEmx2/+ mutants (Figure 5K–O), similar to the LES and IR.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Emx2-/- mutants have no apparent phenotype in the cristae but the outer HCs are absent and inner HCs are poorly organized into two rows.
source: Consistent with the normal expression pattern of Emx2 and these GOF results, Emx2-/- mutants have no apparent phenotype in the cristae but the outer HCs are absent and inner HCs are poorly organized into two rows (Figure 2—figure supplement 2H–K; Holley et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2 and citation to Holley et al., 2010.

claim: The Gfi1Cre/+;RosaEmx2/+ mice survived until early postnatal ages and they exhibited balance deficits.
source: The Gfi1Cre/+;RosaEmx2/+ mice survived until early postnatal ages and they exhibited balance deficits that are presumably caused by the polarity phenotype in the cristae and maculae.
evidence: This is an observation from the study.

claim: Emx2 has a dominant, cell-autonomous effect in dictating hair bundle polarity pattern in the inner ear which is likely to be important for normal inner ear functions.
source: Taken together, these results suggest that Emx2 has a dominant, cell-autonomous effect in dictating hair bundle polarity pattern in the inner ear which is likely to be important for normal inner ear functions.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the gain-of-function experiments and behavioral observations.

claim: Pk2 immunoreactivity in control utricles is always concentrated on the medial side of the HC-supporting cell border despite the hair bundle polarity reversal across the LPR.
source: Comparing the distribution of some of the cPCP proteins such as Pk2 and Vangl2 between control and Emx2 mutant utricles, we confirmed that Pk2 immunoreactivity in control utricles is always concentrated on the medial side of the HC-supporting cell border despite the hair bundle polarity reversal across the LPR (Figure 6A–C; Deans et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6 and citation to Deans et al., 2007.

claim: The distribution of Vangl2 in control utricles is not changed across the LPR.
source: Similar to Pk2, the distribution of Vangl2 in control utricles, though strongest between supporting cells, is not changed across the LPR (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A–B; Jones et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1 and citation to Jones et al., 2014.

claim: The expression pattern of Vangl2 is maintained in the Emx2 mutants.
source: This expression pattern of Vangl2 is also maintained in the Emx2 mutants (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C–F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: The distribution of intercellular polarity proteins in the utricle is not altered by loss- or gain- of Emx2 function.
source: Together, these results indicate that the distribution of intercellular polarity proteins in the utricle is not altered by loss- or gain- of Emx2 function and suggest that Emx2 functions independently or downstream of the cPCP complex.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the Pk2 and Vangl2 distribution data in Figure 6 and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Emx2 functions independently or downstream of the cPCP complex.
source: Together, these results indicate that the distribution of intercellular polarity proteins in the utricle is not altered by loss- or gain- of Emx2 function and suggest that Emx2 functions independently or downstream of the cPCP complex.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that cPCP protein distribution is unchanged in Emx2 mutants.

claim: In control utricles, Gαi immunostaining is associated with the kinocilium and this relationship is consistent among all HCs of the utricle.
source: In control utricles (H–I), Gαi immunostaining (green) is associated with the kinocilium. This relationship is consistent among all HCs of the utricle and the staining pattern of Gαi is reversed across the LPR (yellow line) (I; n = 8).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6H-I.

claim: The staining pattern of Gαi is reversed across the LPR in control utricles.
source: In control utricles (H–I), Gαi immunostaining (green) is associated with the kinocilium. This relationship is consistent among all HCs of the utricle and the staining pattern of Gαi is reversed across the LPR (yellow line) (I; n = 8).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6H-I.

claim: A similar spatial relationship between Gαi and the kinocilium position is observed in Emx2 -/- and Gfi1Cre/+;RosaEmx2/+ utricles as controls.
source: A similar spatial relationship between Gαi and the kinocilium position is observed in Emx2 -/- (J-K; n = 4) and Gfi1Cre/+;RosaEmx2/+ (L-M; n = 5) utricles as controls.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6J-M.

claim: In GOF-SE late utricles, some HCs with normally-positioned kinocilia showed mislocalization of Gαi and Par6.
source: However, in the GOF-SE late utricles, in which the hair bundle reversal phenotype was only partially penetrant, some of the HCs with normally-positioned kinocilia in the medial utricle showed mislocalization of Gαi and Par6 (Figure 6N–O", Figure 6—figure supplement 1M–N", black arrows with asterisks), whereas Pk2 localization remained unchanged (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6 and Figure 6—figure supplement 1 and 2.

claim: By delaying ectopic Emx2 expression until after E15.5, while Emx2 can no longer change the position of kinocilia that has already been established, it can still effectively alter the distribution of Gαi and Par6.
source: Therefore, these results suggest that by delaying ectopic Emx2 expression until after E15.5, while Emx2 can no longer change the position of kinocilia that has already been established, it can still effectively alter the distribution of Gαi and Par6.
evidence: This is inferred from the GOF-SE late experiments shown in Figure 6.

claim: Downstream effectors of Emx2 may normally mediate hair bundle polarity by altering the intracellular polarity complex.
source: This suggests that downstream effectors of Emx2 may normally mediate hair bundle polarity by altering the intracellular polarity complex.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Emx2 can alter Gαi and Par6 distribution independently of kinocilium position.

claim: Blocking the Gαi activity with pertussis toxin (Ptx) or knocking out Gnai3 can lead to misoriented or reversed hair bundle polarity in cochlear HCs.
source: Blocking the Gαi activity with pertussis toxin (Ptx) or knocking out one of the genes that encodes Gαi, Gnai3, can lead to misoriented or reversed hair bundle polarity (Ezan et al., 2013; Tarchini et al., 2013) in cochlear HCs.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Ezan et al., 2013 and Tarchini et al., 2013.

claim: Hair bundle misorientation and reversal were observed only in Emx2-positive, LES of utricles and IR of saccules of Foxg1Cre/+;RosaPtx/+ ears.
source: Compared to controls (Figure 7A–B',G–H'), hair bundle misorientation (blue arrows) and reversal (red arrows) were observed only in Emx2-positive, LES of utricles (Figure 7C–C',E–F, 15%) and IR of saccules (Figure 7I–I',K–L, 46%) of Foxg1Cre/+;RosaPtx/+ ears as predicted by the hypothesis.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7.

claim: No apparent phenotype was observed in the Emx2-negative medial utricle or the OR of the saccule in Foxg1Cre/+;RosaPtx/+ ears.
source: No apparent phenotype was observed in the Emx2-negative medial utricle or the OR of the saccule (Figure 7D–D',E–F,J–J',K–L).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7.

claim: Diffuse or reduced Gαi immunostaining was broadly evident in Foxg1Cre/+;RosaPtx/+ mutant maculae, indicating that Ptx affected the entire mutant maculae.
source: Despite the preferential hair bundle phenotype in the Emx2-positive regions, diffuse or reduced Gαi immunostaining was broadly evident, indicating that Ptx affected the entire mutant maculae (Figure 7C',D',I',J', arrowheads).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7.

claim: Ptx affects the distribution of Gαi in macular HCs, similar to cochlear HCs.
source: These results indicate that Ptx affects the distribution of Gαi in macular HCs, similar to cochlear HCs (Ezan et al., 2013; Tarchini et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7 and citations to Ezan et al., 2013 and Tarchini et al., 2013.

claim: Within the Emx2-positive domain, some Gαi staining was no longer associated with the kinocilium, regardless of whether the kinocilium location was normal or reversed.
source: Additionally, within the Emx2-positive domain, some Gαi staining was no longer associated with the kinocilium, regardless of whether the kinocilium location was normal or reversed (Figure 7C–C',I–I', asterisks).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7.

claim: Only the kinocilium positions within the Emx2-positive domain were affected by Ptx.
source: More importantly, only the kinocilium positions within the Emx2-positive domain were affected by Ptx is consistent with the hypothesis that Ptx only affects the kinocilium position in the regions where Emx2 is expressed.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the Ptx experiments shown in Figure 7.

claim: HC-specific induction of Ptx in Gfi1Cre/+;RosaPtx/+ utricles showed similar but milder polarity phenotypes than Foxg1Cre/+;RosaPtx/+ mutants.
source: First, HC-specific induction of Ptx in Gfi1Cre/+;RosaPtx/+ utricles (Figure 8) showed similar but milder polarity phenotypes than Foxg1Cre/+;RosaPtx/+ mutants (Figure 7).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 7 and 8.

claim: Only 7% of hair bundle in the LES were affected in Gfi1Cre/+;RosaPtx/+ utricles, whereas hair bundle polarity was normal in the MES.
source: Only 7% of hair bundle in the LES were affected, whereas hair bundle polarity was normal in the MES of Gfi1Cre/+;RosaPtx/+ utricles (Figure 8C–D',I–K).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8.

claim: There was no significant change in hair bundle polarity in the LES between Ptx single and Ptx and Emx2 compound mutant utricles.
source: Comparing Ptx single (Gfi1Cre/+;RosaPtx/+) with Ptx and Emx2 compound mutant utricles (Gfi1Cre/+;RosaEmx2/Ptx) revealed no significant change in hair bundle polarity in the LES (Figure 8C–C',G–G',I, 7% versus 9%).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8.

claim: A moderate but significant rescue of bundle polarity reversal induced by ectopic Emx2 was observed in Ptx and Emx2 compound mutants.
source: However, despite the absence of polarity defect in the medial utricle of Ptx mutants (Figure 8D–D',I–K), a moderate but significant rescue of bundle polarity reversal induced by ectopic Emx2 (Figure 8E–F) was observed in Ptx and Emx2 compound mutants (Figure 8H–H', yellow arrows, I, 22%).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8.

claim: Ptx not only blocks endogenous hair bundle polarity within the Emx2 domain, it also rescues polarity effects induced by ectopic Emx2 in regions that is not normally affected by Ptx.
source: These results suggest that Ptx not only blocks endogenous hair bundle polarity within the Emx2 domain, it also rescues polarity effects induced by ectopic Emx2 in regions that is not normally affected by Ptx.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the epistasis experiments shown in Figure 8.

claim: Emx2 requires heterotrimeric G proteins in mediating hair bundle position.
source: Taken together, our results indicate Emx2 requires heterotrimeric G proteins in mediating hair bundle position.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the Ptx experiments shown in Figures 7 and 8.

claim: In zebrafish, emx2 is expressed in half of the HCs, oriented towards the posterior or ventral direction within the respective A-P and D-V neuromast.
source: We found that in zebrafish, emx2 is expressed in half of the HCs, oriented towards the posterior or ventral direction within the respective A-P and D-V neuromast (Figure 10C–C''').
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 10.

claim: Neuromasts of m6b:emx2-mCherry transgenic fish showed hair bundles pointing only toward the posterior or ventral direction in A-P and D-V neuromasts, respectively.
source: In contrast, neuromasts of m6b:emx2-mCherry transgenic fish (emx2 gof), which overexpress emx2 under a HC-specific promoter myosin6b, showed hair bundles pointing only toward the posterior or ventral direction in A-P and D-V neuromasts, respectively (Figure 10E–E''').
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 10.

claim: In zebrafish utricle and cristae, the predicted polarity reversal phenotype in loss- and gain- of emx2 function larvae is comparable to what was observed in mice.
source: Additionally, in zebrafish utricle and cristae, we found the predicted polarity reversal phenotype in loss- and gain- of emx2 function larvae comparable to what we observed in mice (Figure 10—figure supplement 1B–J).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 10—figure supplement 1.

claim: Emx2 has an evolutionarily conserved role in determining hair bundle polarity of sensory HCs and establishing the LPR.
source: Taken together, these results indicate that Emx2 has an evolutionarily conserved role in determining hair bundle polarity of sensory HCs and establishing the LPR.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the zebrafish and chicken experiments shown in Figures 9 and 10.

claim: In controls, a similar proportion of HCs exhibited mechanically evoked calcium responses from either direction in A-P neuromasts.
source: Our results showed that in controls, a similar proportion of HCs exhibited mechanically evoked calcium responses from either direction (Figure 10F–G',J).
evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 10.

claim: In emx2 gof A-P neuromasts, all HCs showed a robust increase in calcium during a stimulus directed towards the posterior, and a corresponding decrease in calcium when the stimulus was directed towards the anterior.
source: In contrast, in emx2 gof A-P neuromasts, all HCs showed a robust increase in calcium during a stimulus directed towards the posterior, and a corresponding decrease in calcium when the stimulus was directed towards the anterior.
evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 10.

claim: Emx2 gof HCs only respond to anterior-to-posterior stimuli, which are consistent with the unidirectional posterior-pointing hair bundles in these mutants.
source: Our calcium imaging results show that emx2 gof HCs only respond to anterior-to-posterior stimuli, which are consistent with the unidirectional posterior-pointing hair bundles in these mutants (Figure 10H–J).
evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 10.

claim: The emx2 gof larvae showed abnormal swimming behavior before their demise.
source: In support of these - hair bundle polarity defects, the emx2 gof larvae showed abnormal swimming behavior before their demise.
evidence: This is an observation from the study.

claim: Emx2 knockouts in both zebrafish and mouse are likely to change the directional sensitivity of their HCs and exhibit behavioral deficits if viable.
source: We predict that Emx2 knockouts in both zebrafish and mouse are likely to change the directional sensitivity of their HCs and exhibit behavioral deficits if viable.
evidence: This is a prediction based on the functional data from emx2 gof zebrafish.

claim: The regional expression pattern of Emx2 in the maculae and its role in reversing hair bundle polarity within its expression domain qualifies this transcription factor as a global polarity cue.
source: The regional expression pattern of Emx2 in the maculae and its role in reversing hair bundle polarity within its expression domain qualifies this transcription factor as a global polarity cue.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the expression and functional data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: HCs in the Emx2 domain normally do not undergo cellular rotation to acquire the polarity reversal pattern.
source: Since distribution of the cPCP proteins in maculae is not changed between Emx2-positive and negative regions across the LPR suggests that HCs in the Emx2 domain normally do not undergo cellular rotation to acquire the polarity reversal pattern, as in the case of ommatidia formation in Drosophila (Jenny, 2010).
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that cPCP protein distribution is unchanged across the LPR.

claim: Emx2 effectors function either independently or downstream from the cPCP proteins.
source: Furthermore, the normal distribution of cPCP proteins in Emx2 mutants indicates that Emx2 effectors function either independently or downstream from the cPCP proteins.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that cPCP protein distribution is unchanged in Emx2 mutants.

claim: The relationship between distribution of cPCP proteins and hair bundle polarity appears to be reversed in the presence of Emx2.
source: However, the relationship between distribution of cPCP proteins and hair bundle polarity appears to be reversed in the presence of Emx2.
evidence: This is inferred from comparing the distribution of cPCP proteins in Emx2-positive and negative regions.

claim: Hair bundles in Emx2-positive domains are located opposite to the Fz expression in cochlear HCs and are associated with Pk in lateral utricular HCs.
source: For example, hair bundles in Emx2-positive domains are located opposite to the Fz expression in cochlear HCs and are associated with Pk in lateral utricular HCs (Figure 6C,E; Deans et al., 2007; Montcouquiol et al., 2006; Wang and Nathans, 2007).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6 and citations to Deans et al., 2007; Montcouquiol et al., 2006; Wang and Nathans, 2007.

claim: The interpretation of normal polarity cues is changed by Emx2.
source: These results suggest that the interpretation of normal polarity cues is changed by Emx2.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that the relationship between cPCP proteins and hair bundle polarity is reversed in Emx2-positive regions.

claim: Emx2 could regulate downstream effectors of the cPCP proteins and alter the intrinsic hair bundle polarity.
source: In a similar manner, Emx2 could regulate downstream effectors of the cPCP proteins and alter the intrinsic hair bundle polarity (Figure 8L).
evidence: This is a speculative model proposed based on the data.

claim: Emx2 effectors most likely mediate the change in hair bundle position via the Insc/LGN/Gαi complex.
source: Extrapolating from previous results (Ezan et al., 2013; Tarchini et al., 2013), Emx2 effectors most likely mediate the change in hair bundle position via the Insc/LGN/Gαi complex.
evidence: This is inferred from the Ptx experiments and citations to Ezan et al., 2013 and Tarchini et al., 2013.

claim: The Insc/LGN/Gαi complex is more important for Emx2-positive than negative regions.
source: Additionally, our results suggest that this Insc/LGN/Gαi complex is more important for Emx2-positive than negative regions and other mechanisms are required for targeting the kinocilium in Emx2-negative HCs.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Ptx preferentially affects Emx2-positive regions.

claim: Emx2 has been implicated in regulating symmetric versus asymmetric cell division in the brain.
source: Notably, Emx2 has been implicated in regulating symmetric versus asymmetric cell division in the brain (Galli et al., 2002; Heins et al., 2001), which could also be a result of altering spindle orientation.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Galli et al., 2002 and Heins et al., 2001.

claim: It is possible that Emx2 effectors could function at multiple steps of a cell cycle: spindle orientation during mitosis and/or basal body positioning during differentiation.
source: Though speculative, it is possible that Emx2 effectors could function at multiple steps of a cell cycle: spindle orientation during mitosis and/or basal body positioning during differentiation.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on the known roles of Emx2 and the findings of this study.

claim: In both maculae and neuromasts, HCs with opposite hair bundle polarities are innervated by different populations of neurons that project to different regions of the brain.
source: Furthermore, in both maculae and neuromasts, HCs with opposite hair bundle polarities are innervated by different populations of neurons that project, at least in the maculae, to different regions of the brain (Maklad et al., 2010; Nagiel et al., 2008; Pujol-Martí et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Maklad et al., 2010; Nagiel et al., 2008; Pujol-Martí et al., 2014.

claim: These innervation patterns could be guided by downstream targets of Emx2.
source: These innervation patterns could be guided by downstream targets of Emx2, and Emx2 has also been implicated in mediating neuronal migration in the brain (Shinozaki et al., 2002).
evidence: This is a speculative statement supported by citation to Shinozaki et al., 2002.

claim: Emx2 is expressed in the LES and IR of the respective utricle and saccule in chicken.
source: Our immunostaining results indicate that Emx2 is expressed in the LES and IR of the respective utricle and saccule in chicken (Figure 9A–B',D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9.

claim: In the chicken lagena, Emx2 expression is restricted to the region closer to the auditory sensory epithelium, the basilar papilla.
source: In the lagena, its expression is restricted to the region closer to the auditory sensory epithelium, the basilar papilla (Figure 9C–D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9.

claim: The border of the Emx2 expression domain coincides with the LPR in all three chicken maculae.
source: Consistent with the mouse, the border of the Emx2 expression domain (green line) coincides with the LPR (yellow line) in all three chicken maculae.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9.

claim: Emx2Cre/Cre and Emx2Cre/- embryos exhibit brain, kidney and ear phenotypes similar to Emx2-/- mutants indicating that Emx2Cre is a null allele.
source: Our results showed that Emx2Cre/Cre and Emx2Cre/- embryos exhibit brain, kidney and ear phenotypes similar to Emx2-/- mutants indicating that Emx2Cre is a null allele (Figure 2—figure supplement 2; Pellegrini et al., 1996; Miyamoto et al., 1997).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2 and citations to Pellegrini et al., 1996 and Miyamoto et al., 1997.

claim: Each hair bundle is comprised of specialized microvilli (also called stereocilia) arranged in a staircase pattern that are tethered to the kinocilium, a true cilium.
source: Each hair bundle is comprised of specialized microvilli (also called stereocilia) arranged in a staircase pattern that are tethered to the kinocilium, a true cilium.
evidence: This is established knowledge about HC structure.

claim: The organ of Corti and the three cristae exhibit a polarity pattern where all the hair bundles are polarized in the same direction (unidirectional).
source: The organ of Corti (sensory organ for sound detection) and the three cristae (vestibular organs for detecting angular acceleration) exhibit a polarity pattern where all the hair bundles are polarized in the same direction (unidirectional).
evidence: This is established knowledge about inner ear anatomy.

claim: Across the LPR, hair bundles are oriented toward each other in the utricle and away from each other in the saccule.
source: Across the LPR, hair bundles are oriented toward each other in the utricle and away from each other in the saccule (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is established knowledge about macular anatomy illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: HCs in neuromast organs of the zebrafish lateral line are oriented toward each other in a 1:1 ratio.
source: Similar to the hair bundle polarity pattern in the utricle, HCs in neuromast organs of the zebrafish lateral line are also oriented toward each other in a 1:1 ratio (López-Schier et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citation to López-Schier et al., 2004.

claim: The directed movement of the kinocilium and subsequent staircase formation of the stereocilia in each HC require an intracellular complex, Insc/LGN/Gαi.
source: The directed movement of the kinocilium and subsequent staircase formation of the stereocilia in each HC require an intracellular complex, Insc/LGN/Gαi, which has been determined to mediate spindle orientation during mitosis in other cell types (Morin and Bellaïche, 2011; Lu and Sipe, 2016; Ezan et al., 2013; Tarchini et al., 2013, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Morin and Bellaïche, 2011; Lu and Sipe, 2016; Ezan et al., 2013; Tarchini et al., 2013, 2016.

claim: Mutations of LGN (also known as GPSM2) cause a syndromic hearing loss in humans.
source: In humans, mutations of LGN (also known as GPSM2) cause a syndromic hearing loss suggesting that the directed kinocilium migration and bundle assembly are critical for hearing (Doherty et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Doherty et al., 2012.

claim: The global polarity signaling molecules Wnts are required for establishing directional polarity in the developing mouse limb bud and Drosophila wing.
source: The global polarity signaling molecules Wnts are required for establishing directional polarity in the developing mouse limb bud and Drosophila wing (Wu et al., 2013; Gao et al., 2011), as well as hair bundle alignment in the organ of Corti (Qian et al., 2007; Dabdoub and Kelley, 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Wu et al., 2013; Gao et al., 2011; Qian et al., 2007; Dabdoub and Kelley, 2005.

claim: Mutations of cPCP components such as Van Gogh-like 2 (Vangl2), Fz, and Dvl, affect the coordinated alignment of hair bundles among HCs but not the peripheral positioning of the kinocilium or the intrinsic bundle polarity of individual HCs.
source: Mutations of cPCP components such as Van Gogh-like 2 (Vangl2), Fz, and Dvl, affect the coordinated alignment of hair bundles among HCs but not the peripheral positioning of the kinocilium or the intrinsic bundle polarity of individual HCs (Montcouquiol et al., 2003; Wang et al., 2005, 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Montcouquiol et al., 2003; Wang et al., 2005, 2006.

claim: Hair bundles are misaligned in the maculae of Vangl2 mutants and the LPR is disrupted.
source: Hair bundles are misaligned in the maculae of Vangl2 mutants and the LPR is disrupted (Montcouquiol et al., 2006; Yin et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Montcouquiol et al., 2006 and Yin et al., 2012.

claim: The distribution of cPCP components such as Prickle-like 2 (Pk2) and Vangl2 are not reversed across the LPR in normal maculae.
source: However, it is debatable whether this complex is directly involved in the LPR establishment because the distribution of cPCP components such as Prickle-like 2 (Pk2) and Vangl2 are not reversed across the LPR in normal maculae as predicted by the polarity of the hair bundle (Deans et al., 2007; Jones et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Deans et al., 2007 and Jones et al., 2014.

claim: All hair bundles were orientated in the same direction and the LPR was reportedly absent in knockout maculae of Emx2.
source: By contrast, all hair bundles were orientated in the same direction and the LPR was reportedly absent in knockout maculae of Emx2, which encodes a homeobox-containing transcription factor (Holley et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Holley et al., 2010.

claim: The defect in Emx2 knockout maculae was attributed to an imbalance between proliferation and differentiation of sensory precursors rather than a specific role for Emx2 in directing hair bundle polarity.
source: This defect was attributed to an imbalance between proliferation and differentiation of sensory precursors rather than a specific role for Emx2 in directing hair bundle polarity.
evidence: This refers to the interpretation by Holley et al., 2010.

claim: Emx2 expression is required to reverse hair bundles from their 'default' polarity in the macula and neuromast.
source: In our study, we show that Emx2 expression is required to reverse hair bundles from their 'default' polarity in the macula and neuromast.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion of the study supported by loss-of-function experiments.

claim: Ectopic expression of Emx2 in HCs is sufficient to reverse the 'default' bundle polarity.
source: Ectopic expression of Emx2 in HCs is sufficient to reverse the 'default' bundle polarity.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion of the study supported by gain-of-function experiments.

claim: Emx2 is necessary and sufficient to mediate hair bundle orientation in vertebrate HCs.
source: Our loss- and gain-of-function experiments in both inner ear and neuromast indicate that Emx2 is necessary and sufficient to mediate hair bundle orientation in vertebrate HCs.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion of the study supported by experiments in both mouse and zebrafish.
